Caprine - Elegant Facebook Messenger desktop app.

summary.one_liner: Caprine is an unofficial, privacy-focused desktop client for Facebook Messenger, built with Electron.
summary.what_it_does: Caprine wraps Facebook Messenger (and Work Chat / Messenger for Workplace) in a standalone desktop window for macOS, Linux, and Windows. It offers dark and vibrant themes, keyboard shortcuts for common actions such as switching conversations, searching, and inserting GIFs, stickers, or emoji, and options to hide names and avatars. Privacy controls let you hide read receipts and typing indicators, and links you click are not tracked by Facebook. It can keep running in the Dock or system tray, and on macOS it offers a menu bar mode, Touch Bar support, and Do Not Disturb respect. Users can also add custom CSS styles. The README states the app is feature complete and that contributions are welcome for improvements and bug fixes.
use_cases: Use Facebook Messenger as a desktop app
Chat with Messenger contacts without a browser tab
Use Work Chat from a desktop client
Hide read receipts and typing status in Messenger
Keep Messenger running in the menu bar or system tray
how_to_run: Install on macOS: download the .dmg file or run `brew install caprine`
Install on Windows: download the .exe or run `choco install caprine`
Install on Linux: use the AppImage, Flatpak, Snap, or .deb options listed in the README
Developer build: see the electron-builder docs; publish with `npm run release`
notable: Privacy controls: hide read receipts and typing indicators, and prevent Facebook link tracking
Menu bar mode and Touch Bar support on macOS
Work Chat support alongside regular Messenger
Hide Names and Avatars option for screen privacy
Custom CSS styles for advanced users
caveats: Unofficial third-party app, not affiliated with Facebook
Several features are macOS only, such as menu bar mode, Touch Bar, vibrancy, and Do Not Disturb respect
Custom spell-check languages are not available on macOS
Menu bar localization is not planned; only the Facebook-provided interface is localized
